doctrine: Strategic autonomy — India seeks to avoid binding alliance commitments, instead building multiple parallel partnerships (US/Quad, Russia, France, Gulf states) that give it flexibility rather than dependence on any single power bloc.
strategic_priorities: Manage the two-front border tension with China and Pakistan without being drawn into simultaneous conflict on both
Diversify energy suppliers to reduce exposure to any single source or route
Build domestic defence manufacturing capacity (referred to domestically as 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' / self-reliant India) to reduce arms-import dependence
Deepen Indo-Pacific partnerships (Quad with US, Japan, Australia) as a counterweight to Chinese regional influence
Maintain independent ties with Russia despite Western pressure, given Russia's role as a long-standing defence supplier and discounted energy source
priority_regions: South Asia (Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal — 'neighbourhood first' policy)
Indo-Pacific (Quad partners, ASEAN, South China Sea-adjacent states)
Middle East/Gulf (energy suppliers and large Indian expatriate population)

cooperation_and_competition.notes: India avoids treating any relationship as purely one-dimensional — for example, it maintains a close US partnership while also sustaining a decades-long Russia relationship that the US does not always welcome.

_meta.data_quality: sourced/analytical synthesis based on India's publicly stated policy positions and widely reported strategic behaviour
